items.problem: A C# UWP app that ProjectReferences a native WinRT component (.vcxproj C++/CX or C++/WinRT helper) has no migration guidance and the bootstrap never surfaces the dependency; the agent spent ~9 turns hand-inspecting the solution and PE-parsing the DLL to conclude OpenCVBridge was AppContainer-flagged before replacing it with managed OpenCvSharp4.
items.evidence: session-log.txt ~lines 1486-2012 (PE DllCharacteristics=0x1160 -> IsAppContainer:True; 'OpenCVBridge.dll is AppContainer-flagged so I'll use OpenCvSharp4 instead'); UWP csproj <ProjectReference Include="..\shared\OpenCVBridge\OpenCVBridge.vcxproj">; lessons.json dev_agent_struggles[0].
items.root_cause: Skill covers C# source + PackageReference reconciliation but not a native-component ProjectReference; bootstrap preserves the UWP csproj without parsing it for native references, so the dependency is invisible.
items.change: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 now scans the preserved UWP .csproj(s) for <ProjectReference> to a .vcxproj and, when found, prints a prominent 'NATIVE COMPONENT DEPENDENCY DETECTED' warning in the BOOTSTRAP COMPLETE block pointing at the new native-component pattern anchor and stating do-not-refuse.
items.expected_effect: The agent learns of the native dependency at bootstrap time (a step it cannot skip) and plans rebuild-or-replace immediately instead of discovering it mid-build.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run of any UWP app with a native .vcxproj ProjectReference, the BOOTSTRAP COMPLETE output contains 'NATIVE COMPONENT DEPENDENCY DETECTED' and the agent does not spend turns PE-inspecting DLLs before deciding to replace/rebuild.

items.problem: Even once detected, the skill had no documented decision for what to do with a native component ProjectReference.
items.evidence: grep of SKILL.md / MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md / scripts for 'ProjectReference|vcxproj|winmd|native|C++|AppContainer' returned nothing before this change.
items.change: Added MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md section (anchor native-component) stating the AppContainer-load rule and the rebuild-or-replace decision (replace with a managed equivalent NuGet + re-implement the helper surface, or rebuild the native component for desktop; feature is adaptable not defer). Tier 3 chosen because the *decision/knowledge* cannot live in a script — the script (Tier 1) can only detect and route to it.
items.expected_effect: Get-MigrationPattern.ps1 -Anchor native-component returns a concrete rebuild-or-replace recipe; agent adapts the feature instead of deferring or stalling.
items.falsifiable_check: Get-MigrationPattern.ps1 -Anchor native-component returns the section; on re-run the native-backed feature is migrated (adaptable) rather than deferred or dropped.

items.problem: The 'C++/WinRT ... out of scope — refuse' clause is ambiguous and could trigger a false refusal for a C# app whose solution contains a native component.
items.evidence: SKILL.md front-matter description line; scenario is a C# app referencing OpenCVBridge.vcxproj. skill-coverage-gaps.json item 1.
items.root_cause: Wording does not distinguish the application project's language from a referenced native dependency.
items.change: Clarified the SKILL.md description clause to say only C++/WinRT/VB *application* projects are refused, and added a short 'Native WinRT component dependencies' subsection routing to the native-component pattern.
items.expected_effect: Agents do not wrongly refuse an in-scope C# app that references a native component.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run of a C# app with a native ProjectReference, the agent proceeds with the migration (no refusal) and follows the native-component pattern.
